Convert a Timestral forecast to a forecast-package object

Source: R/forecast_pkg.R
timestral_as_forecast.Rd

Builds an object of class "forecast", so the forecast package's tools (autoplot(), accuracy(), print(), ...) work on a Timestral forecast. A "forecast" object holds one univariate series: pick it with series and variate.

Usage

timestral_as_forecast(fc, level = c(80, 98), series = 1L, variate = 1L)

Arguments

fc

a timestral_forecast made from ts input, so it has a time base

level

interval levels in percent (fractions in (0, 1) are taken as percentages, as in the forecast package); each must pair two quantile knots (see Details)

series

which series of a batch forecast

variate

which variate, by index or name

Value

An object of class "forecast" with mean, lower, upper (ts matrices with one column per level), level, x (the observed context, NA where missing), series and method = "Timestral". fitted and residuals are all NA: a zero-shot model is not fitted to the context, so forecast::accuracy() reports test-set measures (training-set rows are NaN).

Details

The median is the point forecast (mean). Each interval level L takes its bounds from the quantile knots at (1 - L/100) / 2 and (1 + L/100) / 2, so L must pair two knots of the checkpoint: with the official knots (timestral_levels()) 80, 90 and 98 work, but the forecast package's usual 95 does not, because there are no 0.025 and 0.975 knots. Quantiles are not interpolated between knots. The default levels are therefore c(80, 98).

See also

forecast.timestral_model() to forecast and convert in one call.

Examples

m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
fc <- timestral_forecast(m, AirPassengers, h = 12)
if (requireNamespace("forecast", quietly = TRUE))
  timestral_as_forecast(fc)
